A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Orbit/Orbit+ study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and matchable, including the renumbered appendix sections.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A.6–A.7 report original prediction errors, validation losses, solver objectives, constraint violations, and symmetry-detection measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A.7–A.8 retain original empirical evaluations on BPP, BIP, and SMSP, including prediction performance and solver-related measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Orbit+, and label adjustment using SymILO are retained. Expanded matrix notation and clarification of SymILO's use do not establish a changed algorithm, architecture, or training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same bin-packing, balanced-item-placement, and steel-mill-slab problems. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The experiment-specific comparator sets remain unchanged: No-Aug, Uniform, and Position in Table 2; Uniform and Position in Figure 2 and Table 5; and CPLEX versus CPLEX with Orbit+ in Tables 3–4.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, the 60/40 split, model architecture, training settings, augmentation sampling, metrics, and solver budgets are unchanged. Explicitly stating that all methods use SymILO clarifies previously unspecified coverage rather than establishing a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The convergence comparisons, constraint-violation analysis, and symmetry-detection overhead analysis are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, sensitivity analysis, or empirical case study appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 retain all prediction errors, solver objective values, constraint violations, and symmetry-detection statistics. Figure 2 retains the same curves and trends; relocated appendix results are not new results.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.2 derives the existing isomorphic-consistency condition from assumed permutation equivariance and invariance of a ground-truth function. The original propositions, corollary, and proofs remain unchanged apart from appendix renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about GNN indistinguishability, three augmentation principles, and Orbit/Orbit+ improving prediction and training efficiency.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 and new Appendix A.2 explicitly explain consistency through the ground-truth function's permutation symmetries and how augmentation can disrupt them. This adds a limited rationale; empirical interpretations and Section 6's applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.3.1 changes the vague statement that SymILO is incorporated into 'our method' to explicitly state that it is applied uniformly across all Section 5 methods. This improves reproducibility documentation without establishing that implementations changed.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to symmetry-breaking research and prior ILP/GNN methods are unchanged. Reference entries moving between pages are layout changes.

P1.justification: The revision adds an explanatory appendix subsection, clarifies graph-feature notation and SymILO usage, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, and cross-references. The overall narrative and main section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 revises feature labels and adds an explicit edge-feature annotation; Figure 2 is resized. Tables 3–4 move from page 15 to page 16, with other modest reflow. Table structures and plotted results are retained.

improvement.justification: Explicitly documenting uniform SymILO use resolves an ambiguity about the comparisons, while Appendix A.2 and revised notation make the consistency rationale easier to follow. These provide limited gains in transparency and readability; the empirical evidence and principal limitations remain unchanged.
